title: fix: stabilize CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards during warmup
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes regression causing CUDA graph capture/replay to abort during warmup when shape guards are enabled; improves warmup stability and adds extra validation.
description:
Context: Recent changes to CUDA graph capture/replay introduced a regression during the warmup path when shape guards are enabled for dynamic sequence lengths. In certain workloads (continuous batching with frequent short/long sequences) the graph replay would assert or return incorrect KV cache offsets during warmup, causing warmup failures and degraded tail latency. This PR fixes the root causes and adds defenses and tests.

Motivation: We rely on CUDA graph capture/replay to reduce kernel launch overhead in our serving runtime. The warmup path must create graphs that are replay-safe across the shape-guarded variants we install at runtime. A previous change to how we serialize per-shape metadata and how we apply prefix cache offsets accidentally allowed a stale offset to be used on replay when the captured graph assumed a different guard ordering. The result: intermittent replay failures during warmup (seen in perf-canary and customer Canary on Dedicated).

What this PR does: 1) Reorders shape-guard metadata serialization so capture and replay use a canonical guard index ordering; 2) Adds an explicit validation step at replay time that checks per-guard KV cache offsets against the runtime-allocated offsets and falls back to a safe-call path (no-graph) if mismatch is detected; 3) Fixes a race in continuous batching where warmup and live requests could concurrently mutate the shape guard map; we now take a read-lock during capture and an upgradeable lock during install; 4) Adds unit and e2e warmup tests, plus a small synthetic benchmark to exercise short/long sequence mixes with KV cache hot paths.

Why this is safe: The validation is conservative (falls back to non-graph execution) so it cannot produce incorrect model outputs. The lock introduces minimal latency because capture is already gated to warmup and occurs infrequently; we added metrics to track capture contention. The canonical ordering is deterministic and matches the ordering used by the kernel selector.

Performance: Benchmarks on a p4d machine with llama-2-13b quantized profile show no regression in steady-state throughput and restored warmup success rate from ~88% -> 100% in our synthetic short/long mixed workload. Tail latency improved in canary by ~12% for warmup-heavy traffic.

Related work: builds on previous PRs that added CUDA graph shape guard support (see pr-19681, pr-20322). This PR is intended as a hotfix for the regression introduced in pr-19785.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the guard ordering change and the replay validation semantics. The fallback path is intentionally simple; if reviewers prefer, we can make the validation configurable behind a runtime flag for a rolling rollout, but I recommend shipping the validation on by default for reliability.

review_comments:
Carlos Rivera: 'Can you add a unit test that intentionally misorders guards and asserts fallback is used?'
Author (Asha): 'Added a targeted unit in test_cuda_graph_warmup.cpp; it simulates guard reorder by injecting a different serialization map during capture and verifies replay falls back.'
Marta Ivanov: 'The upgradeable lock looks correct but please add a metric to make it visible in Console.'
Author (Asha): 'Added capture.lock_wait_ms metric and exposed it in the capture codepath. I also added a comment explaining why we don't use full mutex on the hot path.'
Liam Chen: 'CI observed a flaky kv-cache e2e test; can you retry and add a small sleep to avoid race in the test harness?'
Author (Asha): 'CI rerun fixed the flaky test; added a 10ms backoff in the harness to reduce flakiness.'

Final: Approved-by: Carlos Rivera, Marta Ivanov. Marked as hotfix because it addresses a customer canary failure and internal canary regression.
testing_done: Unit tests added for guard reorder and fallback. Integration tests covering warmup path and continuous batching updated. Ran perf-canary benchmarks on p4d; observed restored warmup success and no steady-state throughput regression. Deployed canary to Dedicated pool for 48h (monitored capture.lock_wait_ms, graph-fallback-rate) before merging.
notes: This PR is targeted as a hotfix for customers using dedicated capacity with mixed-length traffic patterns. Ops: if you see spike in graph-fallback-rate after rollout, investigate guard_map churn and refer to ENG-3921 for mitigation steps. Consider follow-up to expose validation failures in Console trace for faster debugging.
